_what: Every narration sentence maps to a span of script/essay.txt, the assembled sources of record for this film.
essay_version: v3 locked 2026-10-24 (v2 plus the user's second 1971 line)
thesis: Each mint year in CENTS marks a moment when what money meant was being changed; melted, the dates vanish into one mass, and inscribed, the value and meaning of each year are continually redefined by participants.
script_target: about 90 s; take A 90.9 s, take B 93.2 s
epoch_convention: Historical present: each year line describes its own year. The film's present is 2026; see essay block [11].

claims.say: Let's explore the stories behind the mint years in CENTS by Rutherford Chang.
Each date marks a moment when what money meant was being changed.
claims.note: The film's thesis, interpretation; approved with script v1.

claims.say: That year copper went to the war, and the cent was struck in steel.
claims.span: Because of wartime demand for copper, the 1943 cent was struck in zinc-coated steel.

claims.say: At Bretton Woods, forty-four nations tie their currencies to the dollar, and the dollar to gold, at thirty-five dollars an ounce.
claims.span: Member currencies were pegged to the dollar, and the dollar was fixed to gold at $35 an ounce.

claims.say: The silver in a dime or a quarter is worth nearly its face value.
claims.span: in 1964 its silver was worth about 93% of its face value
claims.correction: v1 said 'Silver is worth more than the dimes and quarters made of it.' False for 1964: about 93% of face; it passed face value in 1967.

claims.say: People hoard change, coins run short, and the Mint keeps stamping 1964 into the next year.
claims.span: Congress allowed the Mint to continue to strike 1964-dated pieces into 1965.
claims.as_of: Wikipedia citing 1964-65 House reports; CoinWeek; read 2026-10-24

claims.say: Then dimes and quarters lose their silver.
claims.span: eliminated silver from the circulating dime and quarter

claims.say: The dollar can no longer be exchanged for gold.
claims.span: the United States suspended the convertibility of the dollar into gold
the year US currency became fiat

claims.say: Material is detached from value, and the effects reach far beyond currency alone into humanity's fundamental relationship to objects.
claims.note: The user's own line, interpretation; spoken as a reading of 1971, not attributed to Chang.
Placed beside the inflation line; the adjacency asserts no link and no motive.

claims.say: Copper has grown too costly for the cent, and partway through the year the Mint switches to zinc.
claims.span: Coining of the zinc cents commenced on January 7, 1982
claims.correction: v1 said 'The copper in a cent is worth more than a cent.' False for 1982: about 0.48 cents of copper at the USGS 1982 value.

claims.span: No Cent is dated later than 1982.
claims.note: Says where the dates stop, not that CENTS ends; the close follows.

claims.say: In the Block, the dates are gone: 1910 and 1982 are the same indeterminate mass.
claims.span: the physical coins are smelted and cast into a solid 68.56-pound copper block
claims.note: The user's own line. 'The Block' here is CENTS Block Copper, the physical block, not CENTS Block 839969.

claims.say: As inscriptions, the value and the meaning of individual years become indeterminate, continually redefined by the perceptions and consensus of participants.
claims.span: the value of his digital CENTS became permanently indeterminate
claims.as_of: Tinari, On NFTs (Taschen); the line itself is the user's own
claims.note: The user's own closing line, unattributed in narration; 'becomes' made 'become' for agreement, flagged to the user.
